frozen: 2026-11-06, before any Exhaustion Land Phase II (1902-1939) grain, straw or forage value was read, and before any parameter of the fertility model was fitted. Seen so far: the two workbooks' checksums, sheet names, README, fields_metadata, crop_types_data, notes_data, factor tables, the non-yield columns of crop_data (year, crop, plot, previous treatment code, sowing date, plot area) and the e-RA experiment page for rex4 (phase descriptions, no Phase II results). The e-RA page for the separate Alternate Wheat and Fallow experiment (rwf3) was read and states aggregate fallow effects (+0.6 t/ha in the first 10 years, +0.14 t/ha over the next 60); that experiment is therefore NOT a blind test and is used only as a development check. Johnston and Poulton (1977) and Warren and Johnston (1960), which tabulate Exhaustion Land yields, are not to be opened before scoring.
question: Does a soil-fertility state (soil organic matter turnover releasing nitrogen, with non-fertilizer inputs, crop uptake and leaching) predict how past manuring and a legume break change later low-input cereal yields? The existing production response has no memory: every plot in a year gets the same yield.

model.carbon: RothC-26.3 as documented by Coleman and Jenkinson (Rothamsted, RothC_description.pdf): monthly; DPM 10.0, RPM 0.3, BIO 0.66, HUM 0.02 per year; a = 47.91/(1+exp(106.06/(T+18.27))); TSMD moisture factor b (maximum -(20+1.3 clay-0.01 clay^2), bare /1.8, 0.444 threshold, 0.2 floor) with evaporation 0.75 x open pan = the existing Hargreaves PET (declared: the PET is used directly as 0.75 x pan); cover c 0.6 vegetated, 1.0 bare; CO2/(BIO+HUM) x = 1.67(1.85+1.60 exp(-0.0786 clay)); BIO 46 %, HUM 54 %; crop residues DPM/RPM 1.44; FYM 49 % DPM, 49 % RPM, 2 % HUM; IOM = 0.049 TOC^1.139 (Falloon et al. 1998). Rothamsted soils clay 23.4 % (RothC's Rothamsted value), Woburn 10 % (declared, sandy loam), depth 23 cm.
model.nitrogen: SUNDIAL-style coupling (Bradbury et al. 1993): BIO and HUM C:N 8.5; residue C:N declared per crop; FYM 35 t/ha = 3.0 t C (RothC Hoosfield example) and 225 kg N (declared, Rothamsted guide value for 35 t FYM); net mineralization = N released by decomposing pools - N needed by new BIO+HUM. One mineral N pool, monthly: + net mineralization + non-fertilizer input I/12 + fertilizer N in its month; crop uptake while the crop is taking up N = min(remaining demand, r_u x pool); leaching = pool x D/(D+W), D the month's drainage from harvest/soil_water_dual.py, W the root zone's water at field capacity (single-reservoir form of Burns 1974).
model.crop: Grain yield = min(kappa x A0, Y_N), Y_N from the season's uptake: uptake = 23 kg N per t grain (grain plus straw exported) + residue N, residue C = 1.03 + 0.63 x grain t C/ha (the line through RothC's Hoosfield unmanured and FYM barley inputs, 1.60 and 2.80 t C), residue C:N 40. Uptake months: winter wheat Mar-Jul, spring barley and oats Apr-Jul; vegetated (c 0.6) wheat Oct-Jul, barley/oats Apr-Jul. Potatoes (Phase I): uptake Apr-Sep, demand cap 150 kg N/ha, residue 0.8 t C/ha at C:N 25, the rest exported. Red clover (1905/06-1911, plots 5-10): takes no soil mineral N (fixation); 1.5 t C/ha/yr root and stubble input at C:N 15 and 2.0 t C/ha at C:N 15 when ploughed in after 1911. Cowpeas 1905 (failed, ploughed in) and bare fallow: no uptake, no residue, bare. A0 is the existing production capacity (wheat rules for wheat, barley rules for barley and oats).
model.spin_up: Each site starts at RothC equilibrium under a prior mixed-arable regime: plant input 1.70 t C/ha/yr (the RothC Hoosfield 1852 value) plus prior manure M0 t C/ha/yr at the FYM C:N, on the site's climatology (1878-1907 monthly means). Before 1878, monthly temperature and PET are that climatology and rain is observed (from 1853).

fitted_on_development_only.parameters: I (non-fertilizer N input, kg N/ha/yr), r_u (monthly uptake fraction), kappa (climate potential scale on A0), M0 (prior manure). No other parameter is fitted.
fitted_on_development_only.data: spent pools only: Broadbalk plot 3 and FYM-only (the prepared_wheat.json strata, harvest 1879-1925, soil state run from 1843); Woburn wheat and barley, unmanured and FYM-only strata (1879-1900; soil state run from 1877). Plot histories: Broadbalk continuous wheat since 1843, FYM annually; Woburn continuous since 1877, FYM annually (declared).
fitted_on_development_only.objective: sum over the six series of the mean squared natural-log error (floor 0.05 t/ha), series weighted equally; bounded search I 0-60, r_u 0.05-0.9, kappa 1-5, M0 0-3.
fitted_on_development_only.selection: the fitted parameters and the producer's file hashes are committed (output/soil_fertility_20261106/selection.json) before the evaluation is run once.

evaluation.data: Exhaustion Land Phase II (10.23637/REX4-YLD0239-01, CC BY 4.0): cereal grain yields, plots 1-10, 1902-1922 and 1935. Forcing: each plot's 1856-1901 treatment history from Phase I (10.23637/REX4-YLD5601-01), management columns only; Phase I yields are not read. Spin-up from 1856 with the Rothamsted parameters (clay 23.4 %). Weather: Rothamsted observed (on site). Red clover forage is not scored.

metrics.M1_manure_memory: plots 2, 3, 4 (FYM 1876-1881, FYM 1876-1901 with P to 1882, FYM 1876-1901 with N and P to 1881-82): per year log10(Y_plot / Y_plot1). Model against the no-memory null 0 (today's production response): MAE and Pearson r.
metrics.M2_legume_memory: plots 5 and 6 (mineral N 1856-1901, no P or K ever; red clover 1905/06-1911): log10(Y_plot / Y_plot1), years 1912-1922 and 1935; model against null 0. Plots 7-10 (P and K residues) reported, not qualified.
metrics.M3_level: all plot-years: MAE log10 of the model against A0 unscaled; Pearson r; within factor two.

evaluation.qualify_if: M1: MAE <= 0.95 x null's and r > 0. M2: MAE <= 0.95 x null's. M3: MAE <= A0's. All three.
evaluation.confounds_declared: FYM residues carry P and K as well as N; the model attributes their effect to N. Barley and oats share A0's barley rules. Drainage from the dual ledger is low against Rothamsted's drain gauges (development diagnostic), so leaching is likely underestimated.

consequence: No production change from this test alone. If it qualifies, the fertility state becomes the candidate farming-system factor (yield per sown hectare under continuous cropping, fallow, manure or legume regimes), to be integrated into the shared grain -> residents -> reach chain under its own declared step. If it fails, the result is recorded and the capacity layer stays a run-down floor.
scripts: harvest/soil_fertility.py (model), scripts/soil_fertility_fit.py (development fit and selection), scripts/exhaustion_land_eval.py (single evaluation)
